title: Machine-learning-predicted approved drugs show in-vitro Leishmania activity
summary: Two classifiers previously prioritized approved drugs from a screened set; ten candidates were purchased for assays against L. major and L. infantum. Five showed dose-dependent effects; intracellular testing and macrophage cytotoxicity were also reported. Domperidone and dibucaine had prior antiparasitic evidence, so the new result concerns the study’s remaining tested drugs and assays, not ten novel therapies.
ai_technology: Random forest and support-vector machine classifiers
organization: Institut Pasteur de Tunis; Université de Tunis El Manar

evidence.tested: Primary full text describes ten tested predicted candidates, three Leishmania strains, intracellular testing and host-cell counter-assays.
evidence.unknown: Earlier drug-specific literature, concentrations, achievable exposure and clinical efficacy require separate assessment.
evidence.ai_role: Previously trained activity models selected FDA-approved drugs for experimental parasite and host-cell testing.

source_review.scope: publisher primary full text. Material checked for the specific claims stated in the record.
